title: Abdominal Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with chronic bloody diarrhea, LLQ abdominal cramping, tenesmus, urgency, and weight loss. UC is an inflammatory bowel disease limited to the colon and rectum — inflammation is continuous from the rectum proximally (unlike Crohn's skip lesions), limited to mucosa/submucosa (unlike Crohn's transmural). Extraintestinal manifestations: PSC (most specific), arthritis (axial/peripheral), uveitis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum. Diagnosis: colonoscopy with biopsy — continuous inflammation from rectum, friable mucosa, loss of haustra (lead pipe colon on barium enema), crypt abscesses, crypt distortion. Labs: anemia, elevated CRP/ESR, fecal calprotectin, p-ANCA positive. Severity determines treatment: mild → 5-ASA (mesalamine) topical or PO. Moderate → 5-ASA + steroids (prednisone or budesonide MMX). Severe → IV steroids, if refractory → biologics (anti-TNF — infliximab) or JAK inhibitor (tofacitinib). Fulminant/toxic megacolon → cyclosporine or colectomy. Increased colon cancer risk → surveillance colonoscopy starting 8 years after diagnosis.
